documents.title: AI Course Policies and Assignment Guidelines
documents.stance_why: The page lets faculty "choose from pre-set AI policy templates, including no use of AI, some use of AI, or unrestricted use of AI, or to write their own", and stresses "instructors' authority"; it sets no single stance, so it delegates.
documents.summary: Faculty guidance from the Office for Faculty Excellence. From Fall 2026 the syllabus template has an AI policy field with three templates or a custom option. It quotes the Academic Integrity policy on unauthorized AI and citation, and asks instructors to disclose their own AI use.

units.why: The page opens by telling instructors that AI output "reads as authoritative as well as detailed and comprehensive" and that only an informed person can assess it; this is a statement of fact about accuracy, so it is P31 (AI output needs critical evaluation) as an informs rationale.
units.anchor: can well assess its accuracy or usefulness

units.why: "Students new to a discipline are likely to over-estimate AI's accuracy and usefulness" says novices cannot judge AI output, matching P42 (protect novices); it is not a rule, so modality is informs.
units.anchor: Students new to a discipline are likely to over-estimate AI’s accuracy and usefulness
units.frag_end: careful guidance and education to develop AI critical thinking
units.fit_note: Also says novices need careful guidance and education to develop AI critical thinking, which P42 does not capture.

units.why: "will come with a designated field for AI policy" is an institutional set-up step that puts an AI statement in every syllabus template from Fall 2026; closest type is P09, though it is a template field rather than a mandate to instructors.
units.anchor: the Montclair Syllabus template will come with a designated field for AI policy
units.fit_note: The template provides a field for an AI policy; the text does not say that filling it is mandatory.

units.why: The templates "including no use of AI, some use of AI, or unrestricted use of AI" are named levels of permitted AI use, so P05.
units.anchor: no use of AI, some use of AI, or unrestricted use of AI
units.frag_start: Faculty will be able to choose
units.frag_end: unrestricted use of AI, or to write

units.why: Faculty may "write their own AI policy" instead of a template; the rule is decided per instructor, so P04 rather than P05 (which is about the tier names).
units.anchor: or to write their own AI policy
units.frag_start: Faculty will be able to choose

units.why: The university Academic Integrity policy lists "unauthorized assistance or unauthorized materials from any source ... generative artificial intelligence (AI)" as dishonest behavior; this classifies unauthorized AI use as misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: unauthorized assistance or unauthorized materials from any source
units.frag_start: includes as an example of dishonest behavior

units.why: "The emphasis on unauthorized recognizes instructors' authority to establish clear expectations" says each instructor decides whether and how AI may be used, so P04 (not P36, which is about classification as misconduct).
units.anchor: recognizes instructors' authority to establish clear expectations about whether and how

units.why: The policy quote "Cite a generative AI tool whenever work created by the tool is paraphrased, quoted, or incorporated" is a citation duty for students, P24; it does not require prompt or output detail, so not P25.
units.anchor: Cite a generative AI tool whenever work created by the tool is paraphrased

units.why: "If generative AI was used to edit one's own prose, the use of the tool for this function should be acknowledged" is a rule about AI for writing, separate from the general citation rule, so P18 rather than P24.
units.anchor: the use of the tool for this function should be acknowledged in the work

units.why: "Disclose and explain how you use AI to support your teaching" asks instructors to tell students about their own AI use, which is P47.
units.anchor: Disclose and explain how you use AI to support your teaching

units.why: Disclosure is said to model "professional behavior and ethics around AI use" for students; this is a reason tied to teaching professional AI practice, nearest P44, though it is about instructor modeling.
units.anchor: modeling professional behavior and ethics around AI use for them
units.frag_start: Setting an example of disclosing and
units.fit_note: The professional-skill point is about instructors modeling ethical disclosure, not about students learning to use AI effectively.

units.why: The page lists "Citing AI", "Montclair faculty statements" and "a larger national collection of statements" as faculty resources for drafting policies, which is support for instructors in setting policy (P63).
units.fit_note: Resources are sample statements and a citing guide rather than workshops or consultations.

notes: Only one included document. A draft university AI Innovation and Responsible Use Policy was expected in Fall 2026 but is not yet available.
